newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico govt may not stick to Telmex, official says.
newsitem.headline: Mexico govt may not stick to Telmex, official says.

text.p: The Mexican government may not automatically choose Telefonos de Mexico (Telmex) as its long-distance phone service provider in the future, a senior telecommunications official said on Monday.

"I feel that the Comptroller's ministry should issue rules which would oblige the government to obtain the best conditions it can in telephone services," Carlos Casasus, president of the Federal Telecommunications Commission, told Reuters.
Casasus said that current long-distance monopoly-holder Telmex would have to compete with other long-distance companies from the start of 1997, including joint ventures involving AT&T and MCI.
But full long-distance competition serving all of Mexico would not kick in straight away, he added.

"The problem is that until competition reaches all the cities in the country, there can't be any contest, because (the government's) only option in many places is Telmex," Casasus said in a brief interview.
"There could be a contest. It is necessary to make the competition for the government's business explicit," he added.
Formerly state-owned Telmex was privatised in 1990. It has linked up with Sprint to try and fend off competition once it begins next year.
Casasus also said the government has received 27 bids from 17 companies seeking to operate new or expanded beeper services. Winning bidders would be announced by November 12 at the latest, he said.
